## Context / Problem
S2-S5 establish parser-derived help, lazy execution, semantic capabilities, and downstream contracts while retaining derived compatibility exports for safe expansion. RP-05 remains incomplete while the facade or handlers expose parallel policy sets, explicit selection ladders, imperative duplicate grammars, hand-authored usage tables, or manual documentation censuses that future commands can update instead of the authorities.

## Approach
Perform the contract phase after S2-S5 pass.

1. Use semantic navigation plus repository-wide string scans to inventory every reference/patch/import of old policy names, ladder helpers, command registries, parser loops, help-text authorities, and generator compatibility data.
2. Move remaining consumers to route/capability/parser APIs. Delete the 19 policy/census objects, explicit intercept selection ladder, derived compatibility exports, docs-only/manual syntax tables, and command-handler imperative grammars superseded by S2 factories.
3. Preserve specialized handler modules and the selected handler's S2 parser ownership; do not fold domain execution or build a root argparse tree in the facade.
4. Run whole-route and whole-parser shadow comparison immediately before deletion. Fail on any delta except the approved help/overview normalization.
5. Run both generators twice and `--check`; assert every runtime parser ref has exactly the expected committed artifact and reference section.
6. Keep all source modules below 800 lines, split only on existing call-graph seams, and create no file under 100 lines.
7. Document the completed migration and code-only back-out. No ticket/event/bridge/binding migration or cleanup runs.

The positive rationale is to leave one writable route authority, one semantic capability authority, and one runtime-used argparse grammar per command. This removes migration scaffolding rather than adding a feature flag.

## Compatibility and Rollback
All hard-won parser/help/mount/init/output/bridge/optionality/degradation tests remain authoritative. Deltas are limited to S2's approved help/overview change. Before contraction, rollback uses compatibility exports; after contraction, reverting code plus generated artifacts restores the old route because no stored format changed.

## Testing
Run focused real subprocess suites for help/mount/argv/output/aliases/retired commands and selected capabilities, both generator checks, lean/full-extra contracts, and repository lint/type/module-size/complexity gates. Add negative scans proving old policy symbols, imperative command-grammar authorities, curated intercept tables, and retired tokens are absent while registered compatibility spellings remain. The full suite is collateral evidence, not a substitute for behavioral oracles.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] No shipped source, generator, test, or active documentation reads/patches retired policy sets, selection ladders, compatibility censuses, docs-only syntax tables, or superseded imperative command grammars.
- [ ] Every command has exactly one registered runtime-used argparse factory and generated help artifact mapping; both generator `--check` commands pass on a second render.
- [ ] Whole-route/parser shadow comparison reports no unapproved delta in identity, mount/init, argv, diagnostics, confirmation/output, streams, exit codes, aliases, or capability posture.
- [ ] Approved help/overview behavior and all execution/degradation contracts pass through real subprocess and production-path tests after compatibility exports are removed.
- [ ] Module-size, complexity, lint, and type gates pass with no mechanically split file under 100 lines.
- [ ] Migration docs state the completed contract and code/artifact rollback, and no persisted ticket/event/bridge/binding format or data changes.
